  "text": "The years went the way the tides went, which is to say they were in the tables if you cared to look.

Maren's knees learned the eleventh step before the rest of her did. She took the stair slower and left earlier to make up for it. The clock did not mind. It kept the hour it was given.

The log filled. Her mother's hand gave way to hers somewhere near the middle, and hers went on to the last page and off the edge of it. She bought a second book at the chandler's, the same kind, and wrote the date and Wound, 12:10 on the first line, and nothing else. There was nothing else to write.

Erris Kessock grew up and married a Gillan and did not leave. She sat on the wall outside the harbour office most evenings, the way she had at ten, and asked the time, and Maren told her.

"You'll be going up, then."

"I'll be going up."

One spring Maren was late. A fall on the ice, a wrist in plaster, the doctor at Arden. She came back on the bus with the key in her good hand and went straight to the stair without going home.

Erris was on the wall when she came down.

"Ten past?" the woman said.

"Ten past."

Erris looked at the plaster and then at the lighthouse door and then at nothing.

"When it's not you," she said.

Maren put the left glove on. It took her a while, one-handed.

"Someone," she said. "It's only a clock."

She went home. Erris stayed on the wall a bit longer, swinging her heels."
